polities.name: Puerto Rico (US territory)
polities.desc: Ceded by Spain to the United States in 1898; US citizenship since 1917.

name: The 2010s
desc: The decade after the financial crisis. Shale oil makes the United States the world's largest producer. Saudi Arabia turns its surplus toward a post-oil economy.

events.name: US Shale Revolution
events.desc: Hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling, perfected in the Barnett, Bakken, and Permian basins through the 2000s, turn the United States from a declining oil importer into the world's largest producer of both oil and natural gas by the mid-2010s. By 2018 the US overtakes Saudi Arabia in crude; by 2023 it is the top LNG exporter. The revolution collapses OPEC's pricing power, underwrites American foreign-policy autonomy in the Middle East, and — combined with the collapse of Russian pipeline gas to Europe after 2022 — makes the Permian basin in west Texas the most strategically important patch of ground on earth.

events.name: Saudi Vision 2030
events.desc: Mohammed bin Salman's plan to diversify the Saudi economy away from oil. NEOM, the Public Investment Fund's megadeals, the Aramco IPO (2019), and the opening of the kingdom to tourism and entertainment. By 2025 the PIF is one of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds and an active investor in AI, semiconductors, and gaming. The Gulf is buying its way into the post-oil economy.

polities.name: United States
polities.desc: Still the world's largest economy by nominal GDP and the dominant military power. Domestic polarization and questions about alliance commitments shape the global system.
polities.note: The unipolar moment has ended. What replaces it remains undefined.

polities.name: People's Republic of China
polities.desc: The world's largest economy by purchasing-power parity. Industrial base, shipbuilding capacity, and critical-mineral processing concentrated here at scales unmatched elsewhere.
polities.note: The first peer competitor the United States has faced since the Soviet collapse — and the first ever with a larger industrial base.

polities.name: European Union
polities.desc: Twenty-seven members after Brexit. Economic giant, geopolitical actor still under construction. Energy security and defense autonomy are the open questions.

polities.name: Canada
polities.desc: Tenth-largest economy. G7 member. Carney's Liberals navigating Trump-era trade turbulence and the renegotiation of the North American economic space.

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.desc: Engaged in a war in Ukraine since 2022 that has reshaped European security. Strategic partner of China; primary supplier of energy to Asia.

polities.name: Republic of India
polities.desc: World's most populous nation. Fifth-largest economy. Strategic balancer between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing.

polities.name: Japan
polities.desc: Quietly rearming. Defense budget rising toward 2 percent of GDP. The cornerstone of American Indo-Pacific strategy.

polities.name: Brazil
polities.desc: South American hegemon. Founding BRICS member. Major commodities exporter in a world of supply-chain realignment.

polities.name: Gulf States (GCC)
polities.desc: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — sit on roughly a third of the world's proven oil reserves and a sixth of its natural gas. Saudi Aramco is the most profitable company in history. The UAE has become a financial, logistics, and AI hub; Qatar is the single largest LNG exporter; Abu Dhabi's MGX and Saudi PIF are pouring tens of billions into datacenter and semiconductor capacity. Vision 2030 and similar programs are attempting to diversify away from hydrocarbons before demand peaks. Politically, the monarchies navigate between Washington, Beijing, and Moscow with unusual freedom of action — buying Russian oil, Chinese 5G, and American F-35s in the same week.
polities.note: The first region since medieval Venice where a small population has wielded world-historical influence by sitting on a choke point of the global economy.

polities.name: Iran (Islamic Republic)
polities.desc: The Islamic Republic has entered its fifth decade. The 'Axis of Resistance' — Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias, Assad until 2024 — has been badly battered by the 2023–2025 wars. Sanctions-wrecked economy, nuclear program approaching breakout, demographic pressures. Strategic partner of Russia and China.

polities.name: Turkey
polities.desc: NATO member, EU aspirant turned antagonist, Ottoman-flavored regional power. Manufacturing base, drone exports, geopolitical freelance. Navigates between the West, Russia, and the Gulf.

desc: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic spreads from Wuhan. The Federal Reserve cuts rates to zero and pledges open-ended bond buying. A US drone strike kills Iran's Qasem Soleimani. Beijing imposes a national security law on Hong Kong.

events.name: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.desc: The SARS-CoV-2 virus, first identified in Wuhan in late 2019, spreads globally. Seven million dead by 2025 per WHO estimates; the true toll is higher. The pandemic accelerates deglobalization, supply-chain reshoring, and questions about Chinese transparency.

events.name: Federal Reserve cuts to zero and launches open-ended asset purchases
events.desc: The Fed cut rates to near zero on 15 March 2020 and on 23 March pledged bond purchases in the amounts needed, lifting its balance sheet from $4.3 trillion to nearly $7.2 trillion by June. The move made the Fed the backstop of the world's dollar markets, and its holdings kept growing to $8.9 trillion by March 2022 as US inflation hit a 40-year high.

events.name: Beijing imposes a national security law on Hong Kong
events.desc: On 30 June 2020 Beijing enacted a Hong Kong law against secession, subversion, terrorism and foreign collusion. Police then jailed opposition leaders, and Britain opened a path to citizenship.

events.name: US drone strike kills Iran's Qasem Soleimani in Baghdad
events.desc: On 3 January 2020 a US drone strike at Baghdad airport killed Quds Force chief Qasem Soleimani. Iran fired missiles at US bases, and its air defences downed a Ukrainian airliner, killing 176.

polities.name: United States
polities.desc: Still the world's largest economy by nominal GDP and the dominant military power. Domestic polarization and questions about alliance commitments shape the global system.
polities.note: The unipolar moment has ended. What replaces it remains undefined.

polities.name: People's Republic of China
polities.desc: The world's largest economy by purchasing-power parity. Industrial base, shipbuilding capacity, and critical-mineral processing concentrated here at scales unmatched elsewhere.
polities.note: The first peer competitor the United States has faced since the Soviet collapse — and the first ever with a larger industrial base.

polities.name: European Union
polities.desc: Twenty-seven members after Brexit. Economic giant, geopolitical actor still under construction. Energy security and defense autonomy are the open questions.

polities.name: Canada
polities.desc: Tenth-largest economy. G7 member. Carney's Liberals navigating Trump-era trade turbulence and the renegotiation of the North American economic space.

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.desc: Engaged in a war in Ukraine since 2022 that has reshaped European security. Strategic partner of China; primary supplier of energy to Asia.

polities.name: Republic of India
polities.desc: World's most populous nation. Fifth-largest economy. Strategic balancer between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing.

polities.name: Japan
polities.desc: Quietly rearming. Defense budget rising toward 2 percent of GDP. The cornerstone of American Indo-Pacific strategy.

polities.name: Brazil
polities.desc: South American hegemon. Founding BRICS member. Major commodities exporter in a world of supply-chain realignment.

polities.name: Gulf States (GCC)
polities.desc: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — sit on roughly a third of the world's proven oil reserves and a sixth of its natural gas. Saudi Aramco is the most profitable company in history. The UAE has become a financial, logistics, and AI hub; Qatar is the single largest LNG exporter; Abu Dhabi's MGX and Saudi PIF are pouring tens of billions into datacenter and semiconductor capacity. Vision 2030 and similar programs are attempting to diversify away from hydrocarbons before demand peaks. Politically, the monarchies navigate between Washington, Beijing, and Moscow with unusual freedom of action — buying Russian oil, Chinese 5G, and American F-35s in the same week.
polities.note: The first region since medieval Venice where a small population has wielded world-historical influence by sitting on a choke point of the global economy.

polities.name: Iran (Islamic Republic)
polities.desc: The Islamic Republic has entered its fifth decade. The 'Axis of Resistance' — Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias, Assad until 2024 — has been badly battered by the 2023–2025 wars. Sanctions-wrecked economy, nuclear program approaching breakout, demographic pressures. Strategic partner of Russia and China.

polities.name: Turkey
polities.desc: NATO member, EU aspirant turned antagonist, Ottoman-flavored regional power. Manufacturing base, drone exports, geopolitical freelance. Navigates between the West, Russia, and the Gulf.

desc: Trump supporters storm the US Capitol. Myanmar's army seizes power. The Taliban retake Kabul as the United States leaves Afghanistan, and Australia, Britain and the United States form AUKUS.

events.name: Trump supporters storm the US Capitol to stop the election count
events.desc: On 6 January 2021 Trump supporters broke into the Capitol and halted Congress's count of Joe Biden's win for hours. The House impeached Trump over it; in 2025 he pardoned or freed the rioters.

events.name: Taliban take Kabul as US forces withdraw
events.desc: On 15 August 2021 Taliban fighters entered Kabul as President Ashraf Ghani fled; a US-led airlift flew out more than 123,000 people before the last US troops left on 30 August. The collapse ended twenty years of US-led state-building in Afghanistan and left allies asking how long Washington would stand behind its partners.

events.name: Myanmar's military seizes power and detains Aung San Suu Kyi
events.desc: On 1 February 2021 Myanmar's army detained Aung San Suu Kyi and President Win Myint hours before the new parliament was to sit, and handed power to Min Aung Hlaing. The crackdown that followed set off a civil war that still runs, and in 2025-26 the junta held an election without Suu Kyi's dissolved party.

events.name: Australia, Britain and the US form the AUKUS submarine pact
events.desc: On 15 September 2021 Australia, Britain and the US launched AUKUS; Australia scrapped a French submarine deal for nuclear boats. It tied Australia's navy to US and British reactors for decades.

desc: Russia invades Ukraine, and the West freezes its central bank reserves. ChatGPT is released to the public. The CHIPS and Science Act passes.

events.name: Russian Invasion of Ukraine
events.desc: February 24, 2022. Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The largest European war since 1945. Recalibrates European security, accelerates NATO expansion (Finland, Sweden), and deepens Russia's strategic dependence on China.

events.name: Release of ChatGPT
events.desc: OpenAI releases ChatGPT to the public on November 30, 2022. The fastest consumer-software adoption in history — 100 million users in two months. Triggers the AI buildout that will define the decade's capital flows, energy demand, and strategic competition.

events.name: CHIPS and Science Act
events.desc: Biden signs the $280 billion CHIPS and Science Act in August 2022, including $52 billion in direct semiconductor manufacturing subsidies and a 25 percent investment tax credit. TSMC's Arizona fab, Intel's Ohio and Arizona expansions, Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab, and Micron's New York project all follow. The first serious US industrial policy in two generations — an explicit bet that leading-edge chip manufacturing must be re-shored from Taiwan before a Taiwan Strait crisis forces the question. The EU Chips Act, Japan's Rapidus, and India's semiconductor mission echo the same logic. The post-1980 consensus against industrial policy is over.

events.name: West freezes Russia's central bank reserves and cuts banks from SWIFT
events.desc: In late February 2022 the US, EU, UK and allies froze about $300 billion of Russia's central bank reserves. Central banks turned to gold, and the West still argues over spending the money on Ukraine.

polities.name: United States
polities.desc: Still the world's largest economy by nominal GDP and the dominant military power. Domestic polarization and questions about alliance commitments shape the global system.
polities.note: The unipolar moment has ended. What replaces it remains undefined.

polities.name: People's Republic of China
polities.desc: The world's largest economy by purchasing-power parity. Industrial base, shipbuilding capacity, and critical-mineral processing concentrated here at scales unmatched elsewhere.
polities.note: The first peer competitor the United States has faced since the Soviet collapse — and the first ever with a larger industrial base.

polities.name: European Union
polities.desc: Twenty-seven members after Brexit. Economic giant, geopolitical actor still under construction. Energy security and defense autonomy are the open questions.

polities.name: Canada
polities.desc: Tenth-largest economy. G7 member. Carney's Liberals navigating Trump-era trade turbulence and the renegotiation of the North American economic space.

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.desc: Engaged in a war in Ukraine since 2022 that has reshaped European security. Strategic partner of China; primary supplier of energy to Asia.

polities.name: Republic of India
polities.desc: World's most populous nation. Fifth-largest economy. Strategic balancer between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing.

polities.name: Japan
polities.desc: Quietly rearming. Defense budget rising toward 2 percent of GDP. The cornerstone of American Indo-Pacific strategy.

polities.name: Brazil
polities.desc: South American hegemon. Founding BRICS member. Major commodities exporter in a world of supply-chain realignment.

polities.name: Gulf States (GCC)
polities.desc: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — sit on roughly a third of the world's proven oil reserves and a sixth of its natural gas. Saudi Aramco is the most profitable company in history. The UAE has become a financial, logistics, and AI hub; Qatar is the single largest LNG exporter; Abu Dhabi's MGX and Saudi PIF are pouring tens of billions into datacenter and semiconductor capacity. Vision 2030 and similar programs are attempting to diversify away from hydrocarbons before demand peaks. Politically, the monarchies navigate between Washington, Beijing, and Moscow with unusual freedom of action — buying Russian oil, Chinese 5G, and American F-35s in the same week.
polities.note: The first region since medieval Venice where a small population has wielded world-historical influence by sitting on a choke point of the global economy.

polities.name: Iran (Islamic Republic)
polities.desc: The Islamic Republic has entered its fifth decade. The 'Axis of Resistance' — Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias, Assad until 2024 — has been badly battered by the 2023–2025 wars. Sanctions-wrecked economy, nuclear program approaching breakout, demographic pressures. Strategic partner of Russia and China.

polities.name: Turkey
polities.desc: NATO member, EU aspirant turned antagonist, Ottoman-flavored regional power. Manufacturing base, drone exports, geopolitical freelance. Navigates between the West, Russia, and the Gulf.

desc: Silicon Valley Bank fails. Hamas attacks Israel. Wagner mercenaries march on Moscow and turn back. Starship begins orbital-class test flights from Boca Chica.

events.name: October 7 and the Gaza War
events.desc: Hamas fighters breach the Gaza border on October 7, 2023, killing about 1,200 Israelis and taking 250 hostages — the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust. Israel's response levels much of Gaza; tens of thousands of Palestinians dead. The war cascades across the region: Hezbollah rocket war, the collapse of the Assad regime in December 2024, direct Iran-Israel missile exchanges, and the degradation of Iran's 'Axis of Resistance.'

events.name: Starship — full-stack orbital flight
events.desc: SpaceX begins orbital-class test flights of Starship from Boca Chica, Texas in April 2023. At 121 meters stacked — taller than the Saturn V — and fully reusable, Starship is designed to put 100 tonnes into low Earth orbit at a marginal cost approaching kerosene. By 2025 SpaceX has caught and reused the Super Heavy booster with chopsticks on the launch tower, recovered the upper stage, and selected Starship as NASA's lunar lander for Artemis III. Launch cadence by 2026 exceeds the entire rest of the world combined. Whether the Mars thesis is ever tested, Starship has already collapsed the cost structure of space access by an order of magnitude.

events.name: Wagner seizes Rostov and marches on Moscow, then turns back
events.desc: On 24 June 2023 Yevgeny Prigozhin's Wagner fighters took Rostov-on-Don and drove toward Moscow before a deal brokered by Belarus halted them. It was the gravest armed challenge to Putin's rule; two months later Prigozhin died when his jet crashed, and the state absorbed Wagner.

events.name: Silicon Valley Bank fails after a $42 billion run in one day
events.desc: California seized Silicon Valley Bank on 10 March 2023 after clients pulled $42 billion in a day. Washington then covered all its deposits, stretching federal protection far past the insured limit.

polities.name: United States
polities.desc: Still the world's largest economy by nominal GDP and the dominant military power. Domestic polarization and questions about alliance commitments shape the global system.
polities.note: The unipolar moment has ended. What replaces it remains undefined.

polities.name: People's Republic of China
polities.desc: The world's largest economy by purchasing-power parity. Industrial base, shipbuilding capacity, and critical-mineral processing concentrated here at scales unmatched elsewhere.
polities.note: The first peer competitor the United States has faced since the Soviet collapse — and the first ever with a larger industrial base.

polities.name: European Union
polities.desc: Twenty-seven members after Brexit. Economic giant, geopolitical actor still under construction. Energy security and defense autonomy are the open questions.

polities.name: Canada
polities.desc: Tenth-largest economy. G7 member. Carney's Liberals navigating Trump-era trade turbulence and the renegotiation of the North American economic space.

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.desc: Engaged in a war in Ukraine since 2022 that has reshaped European security. Strategic partner of China; primary supplier of energy to Asia.

polities.name: Republic of India
polities.desc: World's most populous nation. Fifth-largest economy. Strategic balancer between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing.

polities.name: Japan
polities.desc: Quietly rearming. Defense budget rising toward 2 percent of GDP. The cornerstone of American Indo-Pacific strategy.

polities.name: Brazil
polities.desc: South American hegemon. Founding BRICS member. Major commodities exporter in a world of supply-chain realignment.

polities.name: Gulf States (GCC)
polities.desc: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — sit on roughly a third of the world's proven oil reserves and a sixth of its natural gas. Saudi Aramco is the most profitable company in history. The UAE has become a financial, logistics, and AI hub; Qatar is the single largest LNG exporter; Abu Dhabi's MGX and Saudi PIF are pouring tens of billions into datacenter and semiconductor capacity. Vision 2030 and similar programs are attempting to diversify away from hydrocarbons before demand peaks. Politically, the monarchies navigate between Washington, Beijing, and Moscow with unusual freedom of action — buying Russian oil, Chinese 5G, and American F-35s in the same week.
polities.note: The first region since medieval Venice where a small population has wielded world-historical influence by sitting on a choke point of the global economy.

polities.name: Iran (Islamic Republic)
polities.desc: The Islamic Republic has entered its fifth decade. The 'Axis of Resistance' — Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias, Assad until 2024 — has been badly battered by the 2023–2025 wars. Sanctions-wrecked economy, nuclear program approaching breakout, demographic pressures. Strategic partner of Russia and China.

polities.name: Turkey
polities.desc: NATO member, EU aspirant turned antagonist, Ottoman-flavored regional power. Manufacturing base, drone exports, geopolitical freelance. Navigates between the West, Russia, and the Gulf.

desc: A gunman wounds Donald Trump at a rally; Trump goes on to win a second, non-consecutive term. South Korea's president declares martial law and parliament overturns it within hours. Rebels take Damascus and Bashar al-Assad flees.

events.name: Trump wins a second, non-consecutive term
events.desc: On 5 November 2024 Donald Trump defeated Kamala Harris, carrying all seven swing states, 312 electoral votes and the popular vote, while Republicans won the Senate. He became the second president, after Grover Cleveland in 1892, to win non-consecutive terms, and his return brought sweeping tariffs and a harder line on immigration.

events.name: Rebels take Damascus and Bashar al-Assad flees to Moscow
events.desc: On 8 December 2024 an HTS-led offensive took Damascus after 11 days, and Bashar al-Assad flew to Moscow. It ended 54 years of Assad rule and cost Iran and Russia their main Arab ally.

events.name: Gunman wounds Trump at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania
events.desc: On 13 July 2024 a gunman fired from a rooftop at a Trump rally near Butler, wounding Trump's ear and killing spectator Corey Comperatore before a Secret Service sniper killed him. The Secret Service director resigned, and Trump's raised fist became a symbol of his campaign.

events.name: Yoon declares martial law and parliament votes it down within hours
events.desc: On 3 December 2024 President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law, and 190 lawmakers defied troops to vote it down within three hours. He was impeached, removed in 2025 and jailed for life in 2026.

desc: Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs hit nearly every US trading partner. Israel and the United States bomb Iran's nuclear sites in a twelve-day war. China extends its rare-earth controls to goods made abroad. A Moon landing is planned for 2028.

events.name: Artemis III — planned lunar south pole landing
events.desc: Planned for 2028. Artemis III will land two astronauts — including the first woman — near the lunar south pole using SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System, fueled on-orbit by tanker Starships. The target region, around Shackleton Crater and adjacent permanently shadowed craters, contains water-ice deposits that could serve as propellant for deeper missions. If successful, it inaugurates the first sustained human presence on another celestial body; if delayed, China's planned 2029–30 landing arrives first. Either way, the strategic meaning is clear: the lunar surface, empty since 1972, will host humans from at least two nations before 2030.

events.name: Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs hit nearly every US trading partner
events.desc: On 2 April 2025 Trump put a 10% tariff on nearly all imports and higher rates on dozens of countries. It lifted US tariffs to 1930s levels until the Supreme Court struck them down in February 2026.

events.name: China extends rare-earth export controls to goods made abroad
events.desc: On 9 October 2025 China required licences for rare earths and magnet technology, even in goods made abroad. It turned the US chip-control playbook on Washington, which cut tariffs within weeks.

events.name: Israel and the US strike Iran's nuclear sites in the Twelve-Day War
events.desc: Israel struck Iran's nuclear sites and generals from 13 June 2025, and US bombers hit Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan on 22 June before a ceasefire. It set a precedent the two allies repeated in 2026.

desc: US forces seize Nicolás Maduro in Caracas. Artemis II carries four astronauts around the Moon, and Starship reaches orbit.

events.name: US forces capture Nicolás Maduro in Caracas
events.desc: On 3 January 2026 US forces struck northern Venezuela and flew Nicolás Maduro to New York for trial. Washington left his deputy Delcy Rodríguez in charge and took control of Venezuela's oil sales.

events.name: The US and Israel strike Iran, killing Khamenei, and a regional war begins
events.desc: On 28 February 2026 US and Israeli strikes killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, and Iran fired on Israel and Gulf states. The Strait of Hormuz largely closed, cutting the Gulf's main oil route.

events.name: Artemis II — first humans beyond LEO since 1972
events.desc: April 2026. A Space Launch System rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center's Pad 39B carrying astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA's Jeremy Hansen on a ten-day free-return trajectory around the Moon. The first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in December 1972 — a gap of fifty-three years. Koch becomes the first woman to travel beyond cislunar space; Glover the first person of color; Hansen the first non-American. The mission is Orion's shakedown cruise for Artemis III, which plans a crewed lunar south-pole landing in 2028 using SpaceX's Starship HLS. Behind the symbolism: the United States has re-established human spaceflight capability to the Moon just as China's CNSA targets its own crewed landing before 2030, turning the lunar south pole — with its water-ice deposits — into the next contested frontier.

events.name: Starship reaches orbit on Flight 14
events.desc: On 28 September 2026 Starship lifted off from Starbase, Texas, reached orbit for the first time and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites before an early Pacific splashdown.

events.name: Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil's runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro
events.desc: On 25 October 2026 Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro 51.79% to 48.21%, the first comeback from a first-round loss since 1988. Flávio refused to recognize the result and sought annulment.

polities.name: United States
polities.desc: Still the world's largest economy by nominal GDP and the dominant military power. Domestic polarization and questions about alliance commitments shape the global system.
polities.note: The unipolar moment has ended. What replaces it remains undefined.

polities.name: People's Republic of China
polities.desc: The world's largest economy by purchasing-power parity. Industrial base, shipbuilding capacity, and critical-mineral processing concentrated here at scales unmatched elsewhere.
polities.note: The first peer competitor the United States has faced since the Soviet collapse — and the first ever with a larger industrial base.

polities.name: European Union
polities.desc: Twenty-seven members after Brexit. Economic giant, geopolitical actor still under construction. Energy security and defense autonomy are the open questions.

polities.name: Canada
polities.desc: Tenth-largest economy. G7 member. Carney's Liberals navigating Trump-era trade turbulence and the renegotiation of the North American economic space.

polities.name: Russian Federation
polities.desc: Engaged in a war in Ukraine since 2022 that has reshaped European security. Strategic partner of China; primary supplier of energy to Asia.

polities.name: Republic of India
polities.desc: World's most populous nation. Fifth-largest economy. Strategic balancer between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing.

polities.name: Japan
polities.desc: Quietly rearming. Defense budget rising toward 2 percent of GDP. The cornerstone of American Indo-Pacific strategy.

polities.name: Brazil
polities.desc: South American hegemon. Founding BRICS member. Major commodities exporter in a world of supply-chain realignment.

polities.name: Gulf States (GCC)
polities.desc: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council — Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman — sit on roughly a third of the world's proven oil reserves and a sixth of its natural gas. Saudi Aramco is the most profitable company in history. The UAE has become a financial, logistics, and AI hub; Qatar is the single largest LNG exporter; Abu Dhabi's MGX and Saudi PIF are pouring tens of billions into datacenter and semiconductor capacity. Vision 2030 and similar programs are attempting to diversify away from hydrocarbons before demand peaks. Politically, the monarchies navigate between Washington, Beijing, and Moscow with unusual freedom of action — buying Russian oil, Chinese 5G, and American F-35s in the same week.
polities.note: The first region since medieval Venice where a small population has wielded world-historical influence by sitting on a choke point of the global economy.

polities.name: Iran (Islamic Republic)
polities.desc: The Islamic Republic has entered its fifth decade. The 'Axis of Resistance' — Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias, Assad until 2024 — has been badly battered by the 2023–2025 wars. Sanctions-wrecked economy, nuclear program approaching breakout, demographic pressures. Strategic partner of Russia and China.

polities.name: Turkey
polities.desc: NATO member, EU aspirant turned antagonist, Ottoman-flavored regional power. Manufacturing base, drone exports, geopolitical freelance. Navigates between the West, Russia, and the Gulf.
